recommendation: Keep the audit as-is and do not restore the HTTP Date-header timezone sentence. Future timezone-discovery changes should build on the CapabilityStatement timezone-extension guidance and the existing FHIR-42971 audit.
issue_request: FHIR-16434 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked to move the default-timezone Date-header text out of the unrelated Support for Versions section to http.html#return, reworded as guidance to return the server default timezone in the HTTP Date header.
initial_application: SVN revision 14192, mirrored as git commit 69bc784817a08f775619849c0e5374d09748b179, removed the old paragraph from the versioning section and added the reworded paragraph under source/http.html#return.
additional_context: The current build includes source/http.html as the RESTful API page through source/hierarchy.xml. Later applied issue FHIR-42971 concluded that the moved sentence violated HTTP Date-header semantics because HTTP dates are UTC/GMT, removed the sentence from source/http.html in b811010c8b85b48fa2419b47a250e5ffba3e3f51, and added server timezone-discovery guidance to CapabilityStatement via the timezone extension. FHIR-42971 is already represented on the combined branch by dbcb00cce4cc9087dd3a64ca872c8b0e1fb40e57.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing the FHIR-16434 resolution text under Managing Return Content would undo the later FHIR-42971 correction; the original misplacement in Support for Versions is no longer present.

related_jiras.note: Applied/Persuasive follow-up removed the moved Date-header sentence and added CapabilityStatement timezone-discovery guidance. Already represented on the combined branch.
